findings.title: Delegated-completion steer after Stop now errors instead of queuing
findings.body: The new plain-send guard at line 4820 runs before the delegated-completion block at 4886-4919. That block can set `dispatchMode = steer_active` on a run that Stop has already reached. The steer then reaches `dispatchSteerIntoRun`, which now throws "is stopping and cannot be steered" (line 3963). Before this change that steer was accepted and its text silently never reached the agent. Is the mailbox delivery path expected to retry or surface this error, or should the delegated case also fall back to `queue_after_active`? I did not trace the caller that sends delegated completions.

contracts.action: Reject a steer (promote-to-steer or explicit steer) into a run that already has a run_interrupt_request turn item
contracts.equivalent_path: stopReachedRun is already used by the restart-continuation guard and markStoppedRun, and the new call reuses it unchanged.
contracts.before_after: Before: a run with status running was steerable until the provider stopped, so the steer was accepted and lost. After: the steer fails with OrchestratorDispatchError, so the command aborts and the queued run keeps its status and hold.
contracts.visible_effect: Promote-to-steer after Stop returns a dispatch error to the client. The queued message stays queued and held.
contracts.failure_mode: stopReachedRun maps projection-store read errors through mapDispatchError, so a read failure surfaces as a dispatch error and nothing is steered.

contracts.action: Downgrade a plain `auto` send that resolved to steer/restart into queue_after_active when Stop reached the target run
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing steer-too-late fallback at 4797-4815 turns a steer into start_immediately when the turn has completed. The new fallback follows the same pattern.
contracts.before_after: Before: the message was steered into the stopping run and lost. After: it queues behind the stopped queue, and the user-send hold release at 5046-5063 clears queueHeld on the held runs. The new run is created without queueHeld because heldRunsToRelease is non-empty (5173).
contracts.visible_effect: The message appears as a queued run after the earlier queued messages, and the queue resumes once the provider stops.
contracts.failure_mode: Reading the projection store can fail, which surfaces as a dispatch error. The guard applies only to deliveryIntent === "auto", so an explicit steer or restart still errors at 3963.

summary: The change adds a stopReachedRun check in two places. An explicit steer into a run that Stop has reached now fails with a dispatch error. A plain `auto` send that would have steered or restarted into such a run now queues instead. Both reuse the existing helper, and the new tests exercise each path with the effect worker drained rather than sleeps. I found one low-confidence question: a delegated-completion steer can still reach the run after Stop and now errors where it used to be silently lost.
